title: Baptism's rite (CCC 1234–1245)
hookLine: sign of the cross, word, exorcism, water, chrism, white garment, candle

lines: A WHITE CLOTH IN A DRAWER.
cards: In some homes there's a drawer with a small white cloth folded inside, and next to it a fat candle that's been lit exactly once. Nobody uses them. Nobody throws them away either.
They're souvenirs of a few minutes at a font, often from before their owner could remember anything. A Catholic baptism isn't just water. It's a short drama in several acts.

teach.b: Day one hundred twenty-six met the water; today, the whole rite. The Catechism says baptism's meaning shows up in its rite, so follow it.
It begins with the sign of the cross traced on the person about to belong to Christ, marking them with the cross that saved them.
Then the word of God is read, because baptism is the sacrament of faith, and faith comes from hearing.

Then a prayer of exorcism, asking that the person be freed from sin and the power of evil, with an anointing; and the person, or for a child the parents and godparents, renounce Satan and profess the faith of the Church.
Then the water is blessed, asking the Holy Spirit to come into it.
The water goes on three times, by immersion or by pouring over the head, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
Those words come from the end of Matthew's Gospel, where Jesus sends the apostles out, in the Douay-Rheims: "baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
After the water, three signs explain what happened. An anointing with sacred chrism, the perfumed oil a bishop blesses, for a person now anointed by the Holy Spirit.
A white garment, because, as Paul writes, "as many of you as have been baptized in Christ, have put on Christ."
And a candle lit from the Easter candle: Christ has given this person light, to be light for the world.
Then, at the altar, the newly baptized are led in the Our Father, and a blessing ends the rite.

how: In the Latin rite a priest or deacon usually baptizes, in a parish church, with parents and godparents present; the family receives the white garment and a candle lit from the Easter candle.

o: the steps of baptism: cross, water, oil, garment, light
a private blessing said over a newborn at home
the first Communion a child receives at Mass

games.q: each sign and what it shows — tap the pairs.
p: marks one about to belong to Christ

s: the white garment is just a nice outfit for the photos
it shows the person has "put on Christ," in Paul's words.
the baptism candle is lit from the Easter candle
a sign that Christ has given the newly baptized his light.
in the Latin rite the water is poured just once
the Catechism describes triple immersion or pouring the water three times.

games.q: the water has just been poured. what comes right after it in the rite?
o: the person goes home; that's all.
an anointing with chrism, a white garment and a lit candle.
games.why: three signs follow the water: chrism, the white garment and the candle, each explaining what the baptism did.

practice: If you were baptized and there's a photo somewhere, on a shelf or in a phone album, look at it for a minute: who's holding you, who's standing around?

If you weren't, or there's no photo, think of a baptism you've seen, and let the steps go by one at a time: cross, word, water, oil, white, light. If you pray, give thanks for the people standing around that font.

wordCard.voice: Baptism's rite. The sign of the cross, the word, the renouncing and the faith, the water three times, then chrism, white garment and candle, each sign showing what the water did. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the Gospels' verb for baptizing, used in Matthew's command to baptize.

carryVoice: Your line: the white garment. The water, then the signs that explain it. See you tomorrow.
